summary: fix(sync): keep names the dependent pass owns out of the flat worker pool, and name the resource on the one silent error path (issue #14)
reason: `sync --resources journal_entries,bank_accounts` sets both `resources` (the flat worker pool's work list) and `parentFilter` (the dependent pass's filter), because a named parent is meant to cascade to its children. The flat pool therefore also ran every named dependent: syncResource emitted sync_start and then failed in syncResourcePath, whose map holds the only flat resource of this API (`companies`), and the early return handed back syncResult{Err} without emitting any event - unlike every later error path. The collector counted those failures and printed them only under --human-friendly, so a machine-mode run of two resources that both synced correctly through the dependent pass reported `resources: 4, success: 2, errored: 2` with no way to tell which two failed (the number recorded in docs/ACCEPTANCE.md). The exit policy never caught it: criticalResources is empty and there were successes, so the run exits 0. Fix, in two parts: the enqueue loop skips any name isDependentSyncResource() reports as owned by dependentResourceDefs(), so a named dependent runs exactly once, in the pass that can actually sync it (`--resources journal_entries` now reads resources: 1, success: 1, errored: 0); and the syncResourcePath error path emits syncErrorJSON(resource, "", err) before returning, so a name that is neither flat nor dependent surfaces by name in machine mode instead of as an anonymous count. Exit-code semantics are unchanged: an unknown name is still an error, and with no successes the run still exits non-zero. Naming the parent (`--resources companies`) still cascades to every dependent, which is what the cascade rule in the command's Long help promises.
validated_outcome: make check green (go vet ./..., go test ./..., scripts/check-boundaries.sh). Hand-authored tests in internal/cli/sync_named_dependents_test.go run the real sync command against an httptest Fiken with a temp HOME, a temp config.toml and a seeded one-company mirror, and assert on the sync_summary JSON line: --resources journal_entries gives resources 1 / success 1 / errored 0 with no sync_error and no flat sync_start for the dependent; --resources companies still gives one flat sync_start plus all ten dependents (resources 11, errored 0); --resources not_a_resource gives exactly one sync_error naming it, errored 1, resources 1, and a non-zero command error. Reverted-behaviour check: on the pre-patch code the first test reports `resources: 2, success: 1, errored: 1` for one requested resource and the third sees zero sync_error events. No live API call was made.
